title: Slice a peeled boiled egg in a hinged wire egg slicer, laid lengthwise in its cradle, and swing the frame back open
instruction: Slice the peeled egg into round slices, then swing the slicer's frame back open, leaving the slices in it.
context: Slicing a boiled egg in a wire egg slicer is an everyday kitchen job (egg salad, sandwiches, salads) that most people have done or watched. The maker (Westmark Justus egg slicer): it cuts "the hard-boiled egg quickly and cleanly into round or oval slices without breaking the yolk"; for round slices the egg lies lengthwise in the cradle's egg-shaped hollow, the wire frame is pressed down through it in one stroke and swung open again to free the slices. The hand skill: the slick egg lies crosswise on a saucer and must be turned a quarter turn and set lengthwise and centred in a 6 mm deep hollow; the frame is taken by its small tab, swung over 95 deg along its arc and driven down through the egg against the wires' resistance (about 9 N at the tab) until it closes, then swung back open past upright without knocking the 11 loose slices out. Two arms are not required.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. (1) Hinged wire egg slicer (like the Westmark Justus, 140 x 80 x 30 mm, die-cast aluminium, 10 stainless-steel wires 5.5 mm apart), fixed on a non-slip mat: cradle 8 cm (x) by 14 cm (y), 2.2 cm tall, centred at x 21, y 4, an egg-shaped hollow 6 mm deep at its centre with its long axis along y; the frame (40 g, bars round an opening 8.4 x 12.6 cm, a 3.0 x 3.2 cm tab bent up at its free end) hinged across the +y end (axis along x, 2.45 cm up, at y 10.4), starting swung open 95 deg, resting on its stop. (2) Peeled hard-boiled US large egg, 5.7 x 4.3 cm, 50 g, lying on (3) a loose saucer 10 cm across at x 13, y -10, the egg's long axis along x. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: 0.25 the intact egg has been seated (axis within 20 deg, horizontal centre within 6 mm, no more than 4 mm above seat). 0.5 a complete closing stroke produces 11 clean round pieces, two of them end caps. 1.0 for the final 1 s with frame at least 85 deg open, all 11 pieces in the cradle, hands at least 1 cm clear and pieces still. In simulation, the closing frame has registered all 10 wires crossing the seated egg, the frame is within 1.5 deg of closed, and final pieces have centres over the 8 x 14 cm cradle no higher than 4.5 cm, speed under 2 cm/s. Score 0 if the egg separates before a valid cut. In simulation this is a 1.5 mm or greater gap between matching weld anchors. In real trials check overhead and side video for position, closure, and final hold, and inspect the end photo for 11 intact pieces and no detached fragments. Interior slices have widest diameter at most 1.1 times narrowest. Superficial nicks are allowed if the egg stays in one piece and the final slices are clean.
reset_notes: Clear the slices out, wipe the cradle and the finger pads, swing the frame open past upright onto its stop, and lay a fresh peeled boiled egg (from the fridge) on the saucer lengthwise along x. One egg per trial. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 20 Hz. Wire spans intersect an oriented egg ellipsoid. The hinge resists closing at up to 1.2 N m (about 9 N at the tab, estimated). After a full round cut the 11 rigid slices' welds become light cling (0.3 N, 0.8 mN m). Before the cut, separated weld anchors detect tears. The model omits small dents and off-axis cuts. The cradle is fixed in simulation, representing a sufficiently non-slip mat.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0, 2,400 steps (approached the saucer but left the egg on it). Scripted demo: 1.0, 785 steps.
